skill.name: modal
skill.description: Guide Modal deployments for serverless Python, GPU workloads, batch processing, scheduled jobs, persistent storage, secrets, APIs, and autoscaling.
skill.summary: Build and operate serverless Python workloads on Modal with practical deployment patterns.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown, framework method names, placeholders, and expected Modal APIs. Confirmed examples expose credentials, log secrets, serve the container root, and use unpinned source.

remediation.issue: A container image example copies a local AWS credential directory.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the directory copy with a least-privilege Modal Secret or workload identity. Never place long-lived credentials in an image or container home directory.

remediation.issue: A public web server example serves the container filesystem root.
remediation.suggestion: Serve a dedicated empty content directory, avoid shell=True, and add authentication when files are not public.

remediation.issue: Secret examples print injected environment values and import a complete dotenv file.
remediation.suggestion: Remove secret-value logging and select only required keys. Use placeholder status messages that never include credential contents.

remediation.issue: Image builds clone repositories without immutable revisions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each repository to a reviewed commit and verify the source before using its files in an image.

semantic_findings.description: The image example copies a local .aws directory into the remote root account, which can disclose reusable cloud credentials.

semantic_findings.description: Two examples print values injected through Modal Secrets, which can disclose secret material through application logs.

semantic_findings.description: Image examples clone mutable repository branches without commit pins, allowing upstream changes to alter later builds.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both build commands clone repository URLs without a tag or commit checkout, so build inputs are not immutable.

content.value_statement: Cloud deployment requires correct images, resources, secrets, storage, and scaling settings. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical Modal workflows.
actual_capabilities: Creates Modal application, image, function, class, and local entrypoint patterns.
Configures GPU, CPU, memory, disk, timeout, concurrency, and autoscaling settings.
Designs batch processing with map operations and asynchronous function spawning.
Guides persistent storage with Modal Volumes, commits, reloads, and cache mounts.
Explains Modal Secrets, scheduled jobs, HTTP endpoints, FastAPI integration, and deployment commands.
limitations: Requires a Modal account, credentials, network access, and responsibility for cloud charges.
Provides guidance and examples but does not deploy, monitor, or validate workloads independently.
Examples may require changes for current Modal APIs, dependency versions, and project structure.
Some reference examples require security review, especially credential mounts, secret logging, and public web servers.

use_cases.title: Deploy GPU Inference
use_cases.description: Plan a container image, GPU selection, model loading lifecycle, endpoint, and scaling policy for an inference service.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Data Pipelines
use_cases.description: Design mapped batch functions, scheduled collection jobs, persistent volumes, retries, and resource limits for data processing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Modal Services
use_cases.description: Create repeatable deployment patterns for images, secrets, APIs, concurrency, observability, and cost controls.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Modal Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal Modal function for [task]. List prerequisites, image dependencies, local run steps, and expected output.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner is testing Modal with a small Python workload.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a GPU Workload
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Modal GPU workload for [model]. Recommend the GPU, image packages, memory, timeout, caching, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: An ML engineer needs a reproducible training or inference environment.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scheduled Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Modal job that runs [schedule], calls [source], stores results in a Volume, and handles secrets, retries, and failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: A data engineer is moving a periodic workflow to serverless compute.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Production Inference API
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a secure Modal inference API for [traffic profile]. Cover authentication, model lifecycle, concurrency, autoscaling, observability, rollback, and cost controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: A platform team is preparing a production service with variable demand.

output_examples.input: Deploy a text classifier on one GPU with low idle cost.
output_examples.output: A deployment plan using a cost-appropriate GPU, cached model weights, scale-to-zero behavior, bounded concurrency, and a protected inference endpoint.

output_examples.input: Process one thousand files every night and preserve summaries.
output_examples.output: A scheduled batch design with mapped file processing, explicit resource limits, a persistent results volume, retry guidance, and completion monitoring.

output_examples.input: Reduce cold starts for a frequently used model API.
output_examples.output: A tuning proposal covering minimum warm containers, image caching, model initialization, concurrency targets, latency measurement, and cost tradeoffs.

best_practices: Pin package versions, base images, and source commits for reproducible deployments.
Use least-privilege Modal Secrets and never print, copy, or embed credential values.
Set explicit scaling, concurrency, timeout, and resource limits before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy local credential directories into images or remote container filesystems.
Do not expose container root directories or unauthenticated administrative endpoints.
Do not deploy unbounded workloads without cost limits, retries, monitoring, and failure handling.

faq.question: What does this skill help deploy?
faq.answer: It covers Modal functions, GPU workloads, batch jobs, scheduled tasks, volumes, secrets, and web endpoints.

faq.question: Does it require a Modal account?
faq.answer: Yes. Running or deploying workloads requires a Modal account and valid authentication credentials.

faq.question: Can it choose a GPU?
faq.answer: It can recommend a GPU from workload requirements, but users must confirm availability, performance, and current pricing.

faq.question: Does it manage cloud costs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can propose resource and scaling limits, while users remain responsible for monitoring usage and billing.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use narrowly scoped Modal Secrets, avoid complete credential directories, and never include secret values in logs or images.

faq.question: Are the examples ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Review API compatibility, authentication, dependency pins, observability, error handling, and security before deployment.
